findings.title: Backup-code authentication can bypass the account password
findings.body: The password verification at lines 121-129 is skipped whenever `credentials.totpCode` is non-empty, while the new backup-code branch takes precedence whenever `backupCode` is supplied. A caller can therefore submit a valid backup code plus any arbitrary non-empty `totpCode` and authenticate without providing the user's password. Backup codes are intended to replace the authenticator factor, not the primary password; this turns a stolen backup code into a standalone login credential. Require password verification whenever this is a CAL password login, independent of which second-factor field is used.

findings.title: Backup codes are not consumed atomically
findings.body: The code is looked up from an earlier user read and then consumed with an unconditional update. Two concurrent credential callbacks using the same backup code can both find the code before either update commits, and both will successfully authenticate; each writes the same remaining-code list afterward. This violates the advertised exactly-once property and can issue multiple sessions from one recovery code. Consume the code in a transaction/conditional update tied to the previously read encrypted value (or store codes in individually deletable rows) and reject the request if the conditional update affects no row.

findings.title: Users in the external TOTP login flow cannot use backup codes
findings.body: When `totpEmail` is present (the signed redirect used after Google/SAML 2FA), the page renders `ExternalTotpFooter` rather than `TwoFactorFooter`. That footer only has Cancel, so it does not expose the new Lost access action and there is no way to render or submit `BackupCode` for these users. This leaves accounts that already use the external-provider 2FA flow unable to use the advertised recovery mechanism; expose the backup-code switch in this flow as well and ensure the credentials authorization path accepts it.

findings.title: Existing 2FA users have no way to obtain backup codes
findings.body: The migration adds `backupCodes` as NULL for every existing user, but this endpoint rejects every user who already has 2FA enabled with `TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled`. Consequently, pre-existing 2FA users receive `MissingBackupCodes` if they choose Lost access and cannot follow the UI instruction to generate codes in settings without first disabling and re-enabling 2FA (which itself requires the unavailable authenticator). Provide a secure backup-code generation/recovery action for already-enabled users, or avoid offering the recovery path until codes have been provisioned.
